ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure 1 is an interannual variation curve of the latitude position of the western Pacific subtropical high ridge line in July-August; the horizontal axis is the years around 1955-1990, and the vertical axis is latitude, about 24°-28°. From the figure, the curve near 1989 is at a relatively low latitude position, around about 25°N, obviously lower than the position of about 26°-27°N in many years. Then reason: the stem states that China's frontal zone is located approximately 5°-8° north of the subtropical high ridge line. Pushing the 1989 ridge-line latitude of about 25°N northward by 5°-8°, the frontal rain belt is roughly near 30°-33°N, close to the latitude of the Yangtze River Basin. Therefore, in July-August 1989, the Yangtze River Basin was strongly affected by the frontal rain belt, and precipitation should be above normal.
